To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed a strategy to amplify FCGR 3A exons and to genotype polymorphisms g.7081 and g.10871, which allowed us to determine their allele frequencies in the Colombian population.
we have designed a specific strategy to genotype the g.708T>G/A and the g.10872G>T polymorphisms in FCGR3 (CD16A), and we have evaluated the effect of these variants in NK cells' ADCC.
the FCGR3 gene (CD16) is a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily of cell adhesion molecules that is expressed on the surface of natural killer (CD16+) cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new strategy for genotyping FCGR3A, a gene associated with defects in NK cells' cytolytic activity.
the development of a new method to genotype these polymorphic variants in FCGR3B and to study their effects on NK cell function.
the development of new molecular tools that will help us understand the role of CD16A in the immune system and the pathogenesis of diseases.

genotyping of FCGR3A variants is feasible using long-range and nested PCR and sequencing, which can be used for clinical association studies in patients with NK cell defects.
